---

## Why this exists

`chatticus-b88c0a` proved the **backbone substrate** in a customer account, including a computerless `pong`. This card is the rest of the matrix. **Read the agent tool list before any live row.** Unproven and unimplemented are different costs. Terminal already burned a live AWS run to learn what `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `chromium_action_executor.py` already say.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (`4142832`) calls the snapshot protocol the **design target, not currently wired**. Do not cite the earlier "shipping design" wording (`48a2c79`).

## Agent-facing tools (verified in shipping code, 2026-09-07)

Live computerless OpenAI tools (`computerless_worker_tools` in `openai_completion.py`): **task**, **read_workspace**, **browse**, **request_computer_capability**. That is the production tool list. Gherkin fakes also emit **send** / **purchase**; those are not offered to the live model.

Host executor (`ChromiumActionExecutor._SUPPORTED_TOOLS`): **browser_open**, **request_computer_capability**. `request_computer_capability` with gate `workspace` is **not** a file or shell tool — the executor only opens Chromium, and only for the **browser** gate.

| Capability | Agent-facing tool? | What it actually touches | Live customer run? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Terminal / shell | **No.** Image has a shell; no tool exposes it. | Container `/workspace` is never listed or exec'd | **Do not run.** Own card: `chatticus-e11c17ed-195c-4ad5-8b06-49d2740d20d4`. |
| Browser | **Yes.** `browser_open` on the host. Computerless `browse` is a different tool: it **authorizes an origin** over HTTP (`POST .../browse/authorize`), it does not launch Chromium. | Real Chromium + `CHATTICUS_LIVE_ROOT` browser-profiles | **Labeled stop `HOST_NOT_RUNNING` (2026-09-07).** Kernel `browser_open` / `about:blank`; customer task PROVISIONING; no `tool.result`. Do not retry until the host-RUNNING card lands. |
| File actions | **read_workspace** yes. **write_workspace** is a capability sink only — no OpenAI tool, no HTTP write route. Host executor has **no** file tools. | `computer.workspace` dict. Dynamo `put_computer` does **not** persist it. Nothing in the agent loop reads or writes the container's `/workspace`. | **Do not run.** Wait on `chatticus-fccc4e9a-b3c6-4a14-9317-d0b0c95231b7`. |
| Approvals | **No** agent tool. Humans/kernel: `approve_structured_operation` / immutable binding. | Policy kernel, not the computer host | Not a Fargate sweep. |
| Spend ceiling | Live model **cannot** call `purchase`. Token spend is recorded on the vendor ledger automatically. | Ledger vs sink ceiling are different | Not a host sweep. |
| Relocate | **No** agent tool. Host packs (`ComputerHostDisk.pack_live_disk`) tar host `workspace/` + `browser-profiles/`. The Fargate host worker **never calls** publish/hydrate. | In-memory `plane._snapshots` in the kernel; S3 packs in tests/CLI | Downstream of `chatticus-fccc4e9a-b3c6-4a14-9317-d0b0c95231b7`. Cannot test until a host publishes. |

**Two snapshot pictures exist and are not wired together.** Recite `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` `4142832`: design target; two file layers; do not delete the library; it is unwired, not load-bearing.

That is why the ACME control-plane workspace map was empty: not a missing bucket on the read path.

It does **not** unblock file actions, and under the dict branch of `chatticus-fccc4e9a-b3c6-4a14-9317-d0b0c95231b7` it never will. 2. ~~Terminal~~ **out of this sweep** — `chatticus-e11c17ed-195c-4ad5-8b06-49d2740d20d4`.

## File actions: the bucket question is decided (2026-09-07)

The predicted file-actions failure now has an answer.

**Snapshot packs live in the customer's own AWS account, and the bucket is created in advance by the published CloudFormation template.** Anthus's `ChatticusSnapshots` bucket serves Anthus-managed organizations only. Filed as `chatticus-bb9084`.

Chosen over having Chatticus create the bucket under the assumed role because the customer can review a template-declared bucket before running it, and because it keeps `s3:CreateBucket` off the role entirely — a permission that would fail `8a25af`'s *"why does an agent product need this"* test.

The **file actions** row here stays blocked until that lands, and it is now blocked on a scoped piece of work rather than an open question.

## Two things above are now settled — do not treat them as open (2026-09-07)

**1. The bucket question is decided.** The earlier comment on this card reads *"whoever creates that bucket (template vs assumed-role `ChatticusComputers` — F-computer will say)."* F-computer did not decide it; the role file did.

`infra/customer-role.yml` has **zero `s3:` actions**, and CloudFormation creates resources with the caller's permissions, so an `AWS::S3::Bucket` inside a Chatticus-deployed `ChatticusComputers` stack fails access-denied. Since the template has to change either way, the choice was made on merit: **the bucket is declared in the customer-run published template** (`chatticus-bb9084`), where the customer can read it before agreeing, and `s3:CreateBucket` never goes on the Anthus role.

**2. This card is no longer blocked.** `chatticus-82dab7` closed after the **live cross-account `RunTask` passed** on development. A computer starts in the customer account. Terminal and browser rows can proceed now; **file actions** wait on `bb9084`.

## Suggested first probe

The prompt that produced *"I can't run shell commands directly in the household workspace"* failed with `STOP_NO_COMPUTER_TOOL`, which was plausibly downstream of there being no `ChatticusComputers` stack to start. That is now fixed and **nobody has rechecked**.

Re-running it is a cheap, high-value first step. Use a probe that does **not** touch `/workspace` — `echo hello` or `uname -a` — so a genuine escalation bug is not masked by the S3 gap that `bb9084` will fix. If it still refuses with a working computer behind it, that isolates a real escalation defect and deserves its own card; if it works, the symptom closes with no further work.

## Tool-list read finished (2026-09-07) — verified in shipping code

Checked, not taken on trust:

- `read_workspace` / `write_workspace` → `computer.workspace` dict (`control_plane.py`). Dynamo `put_computer` does not persist that map.
- Host executor: only `browser_open` and `request_computer_capability`; Chromium only; workspace gate is not files.
- `ComputerHostDisk.pack_live_disk` packs host `workspace/` + `browser-profiles/`. Fargate `computer_host_worker` never calls it. `publish_snapshot` copies the dict into `plane._snapshots` for in-memory specs.
- Live OpenAI tools: task, `read_workspace`, `browse` (authorize origin), `request_computer_capability`. No shell, no `write_workspace`, no `purchase`, no relocate.

`ARCHITECTURE.md` already documents the unreachable shell. File-actions is the same class of row as terminal. Only **browser_open** is a real host-tool live test. `bb9084` still names where **host packs** live; it is not what `read_workspace` reads today. Decision recorded on `bb9084`: do not assume the bucket stores the dict.
